title.en: Structured Output: JSON Mode, Function Calling & Pydantic
title.ta: Structured Output: JSON Mode, Function Calling & Pydantic

description.en: Force LLMs to return structured data — JSON mode, function calling, and Pydantic integration for reliable AI outputs.
description.ta: LLM-கள் structured data திருப்பி அனுப்ப கட்டாயப்படுத்துங்கள் — JSON mode, function calling, நம்பகமான AI outputs-க்கு Pydantic integration.

story_variants.en:
## Vaathiyaar's Data Factory

Vaathiyaar holds up a messy text blob and a clean JSON object. "Students, LLMs return text by default. But your Python code needs structured data — dictionaries, lists, typed objects. Today you'll learn three ways to make LLMs return EXACTLY the structure you need."

### The Problem
```
LLM says: 'The sentiment is positive with 85% confidence'
Your code needs: {'sentiment': 'positive', 'confidence': 0.85}
```

### Three Solutions

**1. JSON Mode** — Tell the API to return valid JSON
```python
response_format={'type': 'json_object'}
```

**2. Function Calling** — Define a schema, LLM fills it
```python
tools=[{'type': 'function', 'function': {...}}]
```

**3. Pydantic + Instructor** — Type-safe structured output
```python
class Review(BaseModel):
    sentiment: str
    confidence: float
```

> **Key Insight:** Structured output is what separates toy demos from production apps. If your code can't parse the LLM's response reliably, your app will break.

## வாத்தியாரின் Data Factory

வாத்தியார் ஒரு குழப்பமான text blob-ஐயும் சுத்தமான JSON object-ஐயும் உயர்த்திக் காட்டுகிறார். "மாணவர்களே, LLM-கள் இயல்பாக text-ஐ திருப்பி அனுப்பும். ஆனால் உங்கள் Python code-க்கு structured data தேவை."

animation_sequence.code:
from openai import OpenAI
import json
client = OpenAI()

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model='gpt-4o-mini',
    messages=[{'role':'user',
        'content':'Extract name, age, skills: "Alice is 30, knows Python and SQL"'}],
    response_format={'type':'json_object'}
)

data = json.loads(response.choices[0].message.content)
print(f'Name: {data["name"]}')
print(f'Skills: {data["skills"]}')

instruction.en: Get structured, validated data out of an LLM. The sandbox has no network, so `FakeOpenAI` stands in for the client (like the real API, JSON mode needs the word 'JSON' in a message). 1) Complete the Pydantic model `BookReview` with fields title (str), rating (int between 1 and 5, use Field(ge=1, le=5)), pros (list[str]), cons (list[str]) and recommended (bool). 2) `analyze_review(client, review_text)`: call `client.chat.completions.create` with a model name, `response_format={"type": "json_object"}`, a system message asking for JSON with those keys and a user message containing the review; parse the reply with `BookReview.model_validate_json(...)` and return the BookReview.
instruction.ta: LLM-லிருந்து கட்டமைக்கப்பட்ட, சரிபார்க்கப்பட்ட data-வைப் பெறுங்கள். Sandbox-ல் network இல்லாததால் client-க்குப் பதிலாக `FakeOpenAI` உள்ளது (உண்மையான API போலவே, JSON mode-க்கு ஒரு message-ல் 'JSON' என்ற சொல் வேண்டும்). 1) Pydantic model `BookReview`-ஐ நிறைவு செய்யுங்கள்: title (str), rating (1 முதல் 5 வரையிலான int, Field(ge=1, le=5) பயன்படுத்துங்கள்), pros (list[str]), cons (list[str]), recommended (bool). 2) `analyze_review(client, review_text)`: model பெயர், `response_format={"type": "json_object"}`, அந்த keys கொண்ட JSON கேட்கும் system message, review கொண்ட user message ஆகியவற்றுடன் `client.chat.completions.create`-ஐ அழைத்து, பதிலை `BookReview.model_validate_json(...)` மூலம் parse செய்து BookReview-ஐத் திருப்புங்கள்.

under_the_hood.summary: Structured output narrows what the model may produce, from 'any text' to 'valid JSON' to 'JSON matching this schema'; strict modes enforce it while generating by blocking tokens that would break the format, and Pydantic checks the result on your side.

steps.title: Free text is hard to parse
steps.body: 'The sentiment is positive with 85% confidence' needs fragile string handling. Your code wants {'sentiment': 'positive', 'confidence': 0.85}. Asking politely for JSON usually works, but sometimes the model adds a sentence before it or a trailing comma.

steps.title: JSON mode: valid syntax, any shape
steps.body: With JSON mode enabled, the output is guaranteed to parse as JSON, but not to have your keys or types: you might get {'mood': 'good'}. You still have to describe the shape in the prompt and validate it afterwards.

left.label: JSON mode
left.code:
valid JSON guaranteed
keys and types not guaranteed

right.label: Schema-enforced output
right.code:
valid JSON matching your schema
required keys and types enforced

steps.title: Schema enforcement masks tokens
steps.body: In strict structured-output modes, the provider converts your JSON Schema into a grammar. At each step, tokens that could not continue a valid document get probability zero before sampling. After '{"sentiment": "', only tokens that can begin 'positive', 'negative' or 'neutral' remain possible if the schema uses that enum.

steps.title: Function calling fills a schema
steps.body: With tools or function calling, you give a function name and a JSON Schema for its arguments. The model returns the function name and an arguments object instead of prose, which your code can pass straight to the real function after checking it.

steps.title: Pydantic validates and types the result
steps.body: Define class Review(BaseModel): sentiment: Literal['positive', 'negative', 'neutral']; confidence: float. Review.model_validate_json(text) returns a typed object or raises ValidationError listing what is wrong. Many apps send that error back to the model and retry once, which fixes most remaining failures.

nodes.label: if not: send error back, retry

under_the_hood.takeaway: Ask for structure at the strongest level the API offers, and validate anyway. Schemas plus Pydantic turn model output into typed data your code can trust, or a clear error you can handle.
